title: resilience-sprint-tooling-and-decision-cookbook
author: Marisol Vega
body:
Overview

This cookbook collects pragmatic decision heuristics, CLI snippets, telemetry queries, and reproducible experiment templates used by SRE during 2-week "resilience sprints". It is intended for oncall SREs, reliability program owners, and platform engineers running SLO-driven capacity and burn-rate exercises across Redwood services (primary examples: inference-gateway, model-router, kv-cache, batching-fanout).

Goals
- Shorten time-to-decision for capacity and error-budget actions during active burns.
- Provide deterministic, reproducible steps for reliability experiments and incident reviews.
- Capture automation hooks and queries to reduce manual analysis overhead.

Scope
- Applies to production and staging clusters for hosted Redwood API and Dedicated pools.
- Focused on SLOs (latency and success rate), error-budget management, capacity planning, incident review standards, and operational tooling integrations (Prometheus, Honeycomb, Alertmanager, rdwctl).

1) SLO & Error Budget Reference Matrix
| Service | Primary SLO | Measurement Window | Alert Threshold (burn) | Oncall Action 
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| inference-gateway | 99.5% p95 latency < 120ms | 30d rolling | 5% burn in 24h -> notify | See section 4 |
| model-router | 99.9% request success | 7d rolling | 10% burn in 24h -> page | See section 4 |
| kv-cache | 99.0% hit-rate | 14d rolling | sustained >3% drop in 6h | Cache warm/rollout |
| batching-fanout | 98.0% tail latency < 350ms | 30d rolling | 7% burn in 24h | Throttle/burst policy |

Note: p95/p99 windows are computed with Prometheus histogram_quantile over request_duration_seconds_bucket. For success-rate use the ratio of requests with status <500 to total requests over the same window.

2) Error-Budget Policy (decision thresholds)
- Green: <25% of monthly budget consumed. No action required beyond monitoring.
- Watch: 25%–50% consumed in the last 72 hours. Engineering lead informed; prepare mitigation artifacts.
- Action: 50%–80% consumed in last 24 hours. Auto-mitigations engaged (traffic throttles, lower-cost model variants), SRE & owner oncall coordinate.
- Critical: >80% consumed or burn accelerating (sustained >10%/hour). Immediate incident runbook and possible capacity preemption.

3) Capacity Planning & Quick Decision Tree
- Inputs: 24h qps forecast (rdwctl forecast), 7d trend, pending releases, scheduled experiments.
- Quick decision flow (for immediate response):
  1. Check telemetry: p95 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, queue length, KV miss rate.
 2. If utilization >85% on worker-pool AND queue length rising -> scale up burst pool (rdwctl pool scale --service $SERVICE --add N).
 3. If spike is short-lived (<30m) prefer adaptive throttling: enable temporary request-rate limit policy for low-tier customers via routing config.
  4. If burn rate of error budget >50% and cost of additional GPUs is acceptable -> engage dedicated burst capacity via reserved-pools (page capacity-owner).
  5. Post-action: annotate the action in incident timeline and create a capacity ticket with cost estimate.

4) Runbook: Immediate Actions for SLO Burn Paging
- Pager receives: service name, current burn %, 1h burn trajectory, top-5 traces.
- Steps:
  1. Acknowledge page and set incident channel (#sre-$service-burn).
  2. Run basic checks:
     - rdwctl metrics query --service $SERVICE --since 1h --fields p95,util,gpu_util,queue_len
     - kubectl get pods -n $NS -l app=$SERVICE -o wide
     - Query top traces: honeycomb query id (link provided in alert).
  3. If tail latency increases and GPUs are saturated -> activate burst pool: rdwctl pool scale --service $SERVICE --add 4 --reason "auto-burst: SLO burn"
  4. If CPU-bound control-plane -> restart coordinator with new JVM flags (see coordinator_flags in Appendix).
  5. If error responses spike with a specific model -> route to fallback model variant: rdwctl routing set-fallback --service $SERVICE --model-id $FALLBACK
  6. If cache hit-rate dropped >3% -> trigger cache-warm job: rdwctl jobs run cache-warm --service $SERVICE --sample 10m
  7. If mitigation engaged, capture metrics baseline for 30m and update incident summary.

5) Incident Review Standard (post-incident checklist)
- Required artifacts for P1/P2 with SLO impact >10%:
  - Timeline with automated annotations (start, mitigation, rollback, end).
  - Root cause hypothesis and evidence (traces, flamegraphs, kernel stats).
  - Capacity decisions made and cost delta estimate.
  - Change/process items: e.g., rollout gating missing, alert thresholds miscalibrated.
  - Owner-assigned action items with due dates (max 14 days for remediation).
- Review structure: 60m blameless review, 15m presentation, 30m actions & owners, publish 1-page executive summary.

6) Reliability Experiment Template (two-week sprint-friendly)
- Name: [descriptive]
- Hypothesis: e.g., "Adaptive batching reduces p95 by 15% at 2x QPS for inference-gateway"
- Success criteria: p95 reduction >=12% with no SLO regressions for other services
- Safety gates: canary traffic <=5% for 24h, automatic rollback on >2% error increment
- Inputs: dataset, traffic profile, cluster size, telemetry dashboards (links)
- Experiment steps (numbered) and measurement windows.
- Artifacts: automation playbook (rdwctl commands), alert overrides, retrospective notes.

7) Operational Tooling Hooks & Automations
- rdwctl common commands (examples):
  - rdwctl metrics query --service inference-gateway --since 1h --format json\  - rdwctl forecast --service inference-gateway --window 24h --out forecast.json\  - rdwctl pool scale --service batching-fanout --add 2 --ttl 60m --reason "resilience-sprint: short burst"
- Alertmanager routing rules we depend on:
  - slo-burn-high -> page-sre -> channel #pager-duty
  - capacity-degraded -> post-to #capacity-ops -> create ticket in Jira with priority P1
- Telemetry snippets (PromQL):
  - p95 latency: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
  - success rate: 1 - sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m]))

8) Decision Recording Template (for audit & billing)
- Minimum fields to capture when taking non-trivial capacity actions:
  - decision_id: UUID
  - service: service name
  - reason: short text
  - action: e.g., scaled pool +4 for 60m
  - cost_estimate_usd: numeric estimate
  - owner: oncall name
  - links: telemetry, incident channel, ticket
- We store these as a single-line JSON in the capacity audit log: rdwctl audit write --payload '{...}'

9) Ownership & Escalation Matrix
- Primary oncall: SRE team on rotation (see /sre/rotations).
- Secondary: Platform -> page platform-lead if changes to routing or infra required.
- Capacity owner: assigned per-service in SERVICE_CATALOG (example: inference-gateway -> owner: @ethanliu).
- Billing approval: if estimated cost > $5,000 for a single mitigation window -> require finance approval within 24h.

Appendix
- Example coordinator_flags (JVM) for GC pacing: -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200 -XX:InitiatingHeapOccupancyPercent=45
- Example policy JSON (single-line saved to audit): {"decision_id":"123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000","service":"inference-gateway","action":"pool_scale:+4","ttl":"60m","owner":"marisol.vega"}
- Quick queries and dashboard links: (internal) https://honeycomb.company/internal/dashboards/inference-gateway; https://grafana.company/d/inference-gateway/slo-overview

Related reading and references
- See SLO observability pipeline and validation docs for instrumentation requirements.
- Refer to the chaos exercise library for failure hypotheses and pre-approved blast-radius limits.
